summary.headline: Milky Mist Q2 FY27 revenue rose 41.6% YoY to INR1,089 crore, with EBITDA margin at 15.2% and PAT tripling to INR77.9 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue, gross profit and EBITDA margin for Q2 FY27, with revenue up 41.6% YoY to INR1,089 crore and EBITDA at INR165.2 crore (15.2% margin vs 14.0%). Growth was led by paneer (value +43%, volume +28%), yogurt (revenue +168%) and ice cream (+43%), with protein products now about 12-13% of sales. Management said milk input costs rose about 11% in H1 and were offset by calibrated price hikes, and that Tamil Nadu milk prices are stable. Net debt stood at INR32.6 crore after IPO proceeds and debt repayment of INR750 crore.

segments.name: Paneer
segments.commentary: Largest category; value growth 43% and volume growth 28% YoY. Production is 100 tons/day against 150 tons/day installed capacity (about 65% utilisation).

segments.name: Yogurt (Skyr / Greek)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 168% YoY in Q2; Perundurai plant commissioned Sept 2026 (INR40 crore, capacity raised from 20 to 150 tons/day), currently producing 35-40 tons/day. Management said yogurt gross margin exceeds 50%.

segments.name: Ice cream
segments.commentary: Revenue up 43% YoY in Q2. Freezers rose to 29,000 from 16,000; annualised throughput INR9,000-10,000 per freezer, target INR15,000 per month.

segments.name: Cheese
segments.commentary: Cheese grew 31% YoY, with volume growth of 26% and value growth of 34-35%. Cheddar capacity is 100 tons/day at about 20% utilisation.

segments.name: Protein portfolio
segments.commentary: High-protein paneer, cheddar, yogurt/Skyr and high-protein milk make up 12-13% of top line, up from about 7% last year. Management said these products carry 50%+ margins.

segments.name: Channel mix (H1 FY27)
segments.commentary: Online/quick commerce 21% (11% in H1 FY26); modern trade 22%; HoReCa 14-15%; general trade 28-30%; B2B about 8% (whey powder only); exports about 4%.

segments.name: Geography (H1 FY27)
segments.commentary: South India about 70% of revenue; Tamil Nadu about 26%, Karnataka about 23%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects growth of 40%+ to continue into the next quarter, with value growth exceeding volume growth by about 10-12 points.
Management said it can sustain the roughly 15% EBITDA margin in H2 FY27.
Price hikes of about 10-11.5% were taken across Q4 FY26 to Q2 FY27; Q2 realised price impact was only about 1.5-2%, with the full effect expected in Q3.
Protein products are expected to rise from 12% to 18-20% of top line over the next 2-3 years.
Paneer capacity expected to hit maximum in 24-30 months; a further 200 tons/day paneer plant at Perundurai (total 350 tons/day) is under design.

No major capex capitalisation planned for FY27 beyond about INR70 crore CWIP; Maharashtra plant (Baramati, 50 acres) is at design and approval stage, operational in about 3 years, funded internally with small cash capex initially.
Ice cream expected to grow 35-40% across all quarters; freezer throughput target INR15,000 per month.
capex_capacity: Paneer: 100 tons/day produced against 150 tons/day installed; about 65% utilisation. Plans for another 200 tons/day at Perundurai, which would bring total to 350 tons/day.
Yogurt: new Skyr/Greek yogurt facility at Perundurai commissioned Sept 2026 (INR40 crore, ultrafiltration), capacity raised from 20 to 150 tons/day; current output 35-40 tons/day.
Cheddar cheese: 100 tons/day capacity at about 20% utilisation; management targets roughly 50% utilisation in 2-3 years.

Baramati, Maharashtra: 50 acres acquired; facility targeted for operation in about 3 years. Milk procurement ramp-up in Maharashtra: 25 bulk milk chillers now, about 70 by year-end, procuring 65,000-70,000 litres/day rising to 1 lakh/day by year-end.
H1 FY27 capex about INR240 crore per the analyst's reading of the cash flow; management said cash capex was about INR50 crore of INR144 crore capitalisation from CWIP.
demand_pricing: Milk procurement in H1 FY27 was 246.5 million litres, up 31% YoY, from a network of over 92,000 farmers (up from 75,000).

Milk input costs rose about 11% in H1 FY27 (milk and packaging), offset by calibrated price increases. Tamil Nadu milk prices are seen as stable after recent rains; Karnataka milk price rose by INR4-7/litre.
Management said it could absorb a further 5% milk price rise. If procurement prices fall INR5-10/litre, it would pass through a 2-5% price reduction selectively.
Competition in high-protein: management said the category is early and high-margin, and the market (INR31,000 crore) is large relative to Milky Mist's roughly INR400 crore protein sales.
Lactose-free high-protein milk (250 ml, 25 g protein, 6-month shelf life via ultrafiltration) launched Oct 2026 at INR99 per 250 ml, aimed at modern trade, quick commerce and A-class outlets.
Distribution: about 4 lakh retail touchpoints, 4,200 distributors (200 added), over 45,000 Visi coolers and freezers.

Regulatory scrutiny on analogue paneer and quick-commerce dark-store storage: management said South India paneer is fully branded and it commands over 65% of branded market; organised share of paneer is about 10%, expected to reach 25-30%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the salience of the four high-protein SKUs, and how do their margins compare with the base business?
qa_highlights.answer: Protein is about 12% of top line now and is expected to reach 18-20% over 2-3 years. Biswajit Mishra said yogurt and ice cream carry the highest margins and protein categories match yogurt levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is milk inflation in H1 and H2, and will further price hikes be needed?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 milk and packaging inflation was about 11%, offset with price increases. Management sees limited milk price inflation in H2, with Tamil Nadu prices flat, and expects 15% EBITDA margins to be sustained.

qa_highlights.question: Clarification on price hikes timing.
qa_highlights.answer: Mishra said the H1-on-H1 price increase was 11.5%; Q2 hike was near 10% but only 1.5-2% was realised in Q2, with the rest expected in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cheddar cheese capacity be absorbed?
qa_highlights.answer: Cheddar is an input for processed cheese; capacity is 100 tons/day at 20% utilisation. Management also plans to use surplus milk for cheese and ripening and is developing snack variants.

qa_highlights.question: Growth split between volume, price and distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Weighted volume growth is about 28-30% and value growth is about 42%. Management said growth comes from existing markets and new markets such as UP and Bihar, with distributors up 200 and about 40,000 new retail touchpoints.

qa_highlights.question: Will raw material price softening lead to price cuts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the volume-value gap of 10-12% will persist and volume is the focus. Price cuts would be calibrated at 2-5% if procurement prices fall INR5-10/litre; Mishra said product mix contributes about 5% of value growth.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Baramati plant's milk supply planned, and what is the outlook for procurement prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to run Baramati at 40% utilisation on day one, with milk procurement scaled to 2-3 lakh litres/day before commissioning. It does not expect milk prices to soften soon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk of concentrated procurement in Tamil Nadu (about 85%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said procurement now spans Karnataka, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh, with about 30% of milk expected from Karnataka and Maharashtra. Buffalo milk is absent in South; 97-98% is cow milk.

risks_watch: Milk procurement cost cycle: management sees no near-term softening in procurement prices, Karnataka milk price up INR4-7/litre, and El Nino/summer deficit effects; watch whether the ~11% H1 input inflation persists into H2 and whether the 15% EBITDA margin holds.
Price-realisation lag: Q2 hike was near 10% but only 1.5-2% realised in Q2, with the rest expected in Q3; verify the Q3 impact and the volume-value gap of 10-12 points.

Concentration risk: about 85% of procurement is from Tamil Nadu per the analyst question; management says ~30% of milk will come from Karnataka and Maharashtra over time, and Baramati is about 3 years away.

Utilisation and capex: paneer at about 65% utilisation, cheddar at about 20%, yogurt at 35-40 tons/day against 150 tons/day; watch the 200 tons/day Perundurai paneer plant and Baramati approval/capex timing.

Competition and regulation in high-protein and quick commerce: management said the category is early and expects more brands, but also flagged dark-store storage and cleanliness scrutiny and analogue paneer enforcement; the protein margin claim (50%+) is management's and not yet audited by segment.
key_quotes: We will be able to sustain the current growth in H1 growth and we will be able to sustain the 15% EBITDA margins also going forward.
So we don't see much increase in milk prices.
We see this as one of the strong emerging category in the coming years, at least next 2 to 3 years.
The current capacity utilization stands at close to 65%, but we still have a larger headroom to increase the production within our existing capacity.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, growth (40%+ expected to continue) and margins (15% EBITDA sustained in H2), but noticeably more cautious on milk procurement prices, which management said it does not expect to soften soon. Management was evasive or deferred on some specifics (e.g., Baramati capex amount, exact channel margins, and cash capex versus CWIP capitalisation), and clarified several numbers under analyst questioning.

rows.why: Management says it can sustain ~15% EBITDA margin in H2 FY27 (Q2 at 15.2% vs 14.0%), and the full Q3 effect of 10-11.5% price hikes is still to flow through with only 1.5-2% realised in Q2, though ~11% H1 milk and packaging inflation is a risk.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Perundurai yogurt line (INR40 crore) was commissioned Sept 2026, raising capacity from 20 to 150 tons/day with output at only 35-40 tons/day; the 200 t/day paneer plant is still at exploration and Baramati is about 3 years out.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident on 40%+ growth and 15% EBITDA margin, and Q3 price realisation (remaining ~8-9 points of the ~10-11.5% hikes) is still to come, but milk inflation and the ~10-12 point volume-value gap cap the upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Milk input costs rose ~11% in H1 with no softening expected soon (Karnataka up INR4-7/litre), so 15% margin depends on pricing catching up; Q3 realisation of the remaining price hikes is the swing factor.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Lactose-free high-protein milk (250 ml, 25 g protein) launched Oct 2026 at INR99 per 250 ml for modern trade, quick commerce and A-class outlets; protein is 12-13% of sales, targeting 18-20% in 2-3 years.

rows.label: Expansion into UP and Bihar
rows.why: Growth is coming from new markets such as UP and Bihar alongside 200 new distributors (4,200 total) and about 40,000 new retail touchpoints.

rows.label: Ice cream freezer throughput ramp
rows.why: Freezers rose to 29,000 from 16,000 with ice cream revenue +43% YoY; management guides 35-40% growth across all quarters and a target of INR15,000 per freezer per month versus INR9,000-10,000 now.
